Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the 24 * rule for deciding when two owners denote the same person lives in one place, as pure functions 25 * with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, 26 * {@link EmailNormalizer} and {@link Soundex}, whose comparison keys it composes. 27 * 28 *

The key is the SHA-256 hex digest of the owner's normalized telephone, lower-cased email (or 29 * the empty string when absent) and the {@linkplain Soundex#soundex Soundex} of their last name, 30 * joined with {@code '|'} separators before hashing: 31 * {@code sha256hex(normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName))}. Two owners 32 * are the same, and a create is rejected as a {@code 409 Conflict}, only when their whole keys are 33 * equal — so the previously separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are all 34 * subsumed by this one key. Because the telephone is part of the key, two owners who share a last 35 * name and postcode but carry different telephones have different keys: they are not a hard 36 * duplicate but a {@linkplain OwnerIdentity soft match}. Only an exact full-key match is a 37 * duplicate. 38 */ 39 public abstract class OwnerIdentity { 40 41 /** Separates the telephone, email and last-name components hashed into the key. */ 42 private static final String SEPARATOR = "|"; 43 44 /** 45 * Builds the identity key from an owner's raw parts. The telephone and email are reduced to 46 * their {@linkplain TelephoneNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} / 47 * {@linkplain EmailNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} forms and the last name to its 48 * {@linkplain Soundex#soundex Soundex} code so values stored in different shapes still compose 49 * equal keys; an absent (null or blank) email contributes the empty string, and an absent last 50 * name codes to the empty string. The joined parts are then reduced to a 51 * {@linkplain Sha256#hex SHA-256} hex digest. 52 * 53 * @param telephone the owner's telephone (normalized on create), or null 54 * @param email the owner's email (lower-cased on create), or null/blank when absent 55 * @param lastName the owner's last name, or null 56 * @return the owner's identity key, a 64-character lower-case hex SHA-256 digest 57 */ 58 public static String identityKey(String telephone, String email, String lastName) { 59 String telephonePart = telephone == null ? "" : TelephoneNormalizer.toComparisonKey(telephone); 60 String emailPart = (email == null || email.isBlank()) ? "" : EmailNormalizer.toComparisonKey(email); 61 String lastNamePart = Soundex.soundex(lastName); 62 return Sha256.hex(telephonePart + SEPARATOR + emailPart + SEPARATOR + lastNamePart); 63 } 64 65 /** 66 * Builds the identity key from a persisted owner's stored telephone, email and last name. 67 * 68 * @param owner the owner (non-null) 69 * @return the owner's identity key 70 */ 71 public static String identityKey(Owner owner) { 72 return identityKey(owner.getTelephone(), owner.getEmail(), owner.getLastName()); 73 } 74 75 } 76

1 /* 2 * Copyright 2016-2017 the original author or authors. 3 * 4 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); 5 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. 6 * You may obtain a copy of the License at 7 * 8 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 9 * 10 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software 11 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, 12 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. 13 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and 14 * limitations under the License. 15 */ 16 17 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util; 18 19 import java.util.Locale; 20 21 /** 22 * Comparison of owner households, an owner's {@code lastName} together with their {@code postcode}. 23 * Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the rule for deciding when 24 * two owners belong to the same household lives in one place, as pure functions with no web or 25 * persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, which does the same for telephones. 26 * 27 *

Two owners share a household when their {@linkplain #toComparisonKey(String, String) comparison 28 * keys} are equal. The last name is reduced for comparison by trimming, collapsing every run of 29 * whitespace to a single space and lower-casing, so households recorded in different letter cases or 30 * with incidental spacing still compare equal (e.g. {@code " Franklin "} / {@code "2000"} matches 31 * {@code "franklin"} / {@code "2000"}); the postcode is a fixed 4-digit code and is compared as 32 * given. 33 */ 34 public abstract class HouseholdNormalizer { 35 36 /** A run of one or more whitespace characters, collapsed to a single space for comparison. */ 37 private static final String WHITESPACE_RUN = "\\s+"; 38 39 /** Separates the normalized {@code lastName} and {@code postcode} in a key. */ 40 private static final String KEY_SEPARATOR = "|"; 41 42 /** The number of leading hex characters of the digest kept as the household id. */ 43 private static final int HOUSEHOLD_ID_LENGTH = 12; 44 45 /** 46 * The key used to decide whether two owners belong to the same household: their normalized 47 * {@code lastName} and {@code postcode} joined together, so households stored in different letter 48 * cases or with incidental whitespace still compare equal. 49 * 50 * @param lastName the owner's last name (non-null) 51 * @param postcode the owner's postcode, or null when absent 52 * @return the comparison key 53 */ 54 public static String toComparisonKey(String lastName, String postcode) { 55 return normalizeField(lastName) + KEY_SEPARATOR + (postcode == null ? "" : postcode); 56 } 57 58 /** 59 * A stable, shared identifier for the household an owner belongs to. It is a pure function of the 60 * {@linkplain #toComparisonKey(String, String) comparison key}, so every owner with the same 61 * {@code lastName} (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) and {@code postcode} 62 * derives the same identifier without any coordination or stored state, and the identifier stays 63 * the same across restarts. The value is the first {@value #HOUSEHOLD_ID_LENGTH} hex characters 64 * of the SHA-256 of the comparison key. 65 * 66 * @param lastName the owner's last name (non-null) 67 * @param postcode the owner's postcode, or null when absent 68 * @return the household's stable shared identifier 69 */ 70 public static String toHouseholdId(String lastName, String postcode) { 71 return Sha256.hex(toComparisonKey(lastName, postcode)).substring(0, HOUSEHOLD_ID_LENGTH); 72 } 73 74 /** 75 * Reduce a single household field to its comparison form: trimmed, every run of whitespace 76 * collapsed to a single space, and lower-cased. 77 * 78 * @param field a household field (non-null) 79 * @return the field's comparison form 80 */ 81 private static String normalizeField(String field) { 82 return field.trim().replaceAll(WHITESPACE_RUN, " ").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT); 83 } 84 85 } 86

The restructuring is done. Here's what I did and why.

## What I found

The only test in the suite is `AcceptanceTest.coreV2GroupsIdentityAndVersions` — and it's the **acceptance test for the upcoming change** (it asserts `apiVersion: 2` and a nested `identity` object that don't exist yet). It fails now and will keep failing until the change itself is implemented, which is out of scope here. There are no currently-passing tests to protect, so my bar was: **change zero behavior** (verified against a golden owner response) and leave that test failing on the exact same assertion.

## What I restructured

The V2 change folds a fixed `'V2'` tag into *what each identifier hashes* (`memberId`, `identityKey`, `householdId`). I noticed the three identifier builders were structurally inconsistent: `HouseholdNormalizer.toHouseholdId` already composes its hashed value through a single named seam (`toComparisonKey`), but `MemberId.hash8` and `OwnerIdentity.identityKey` built theirs inline. So:

- **`MemberId`** — extracted the digest input into a private `hashInput(telephone, lastName)`; `hash8` now hashes/slices its result.
- **`OwnerIdentity`** — extracted the digest input into a private `hashInput(telephone, email, lastName)`; `identityKey` now just hashes its result.
- **`HouseholdNormalizer`** — left as-is; its `toComparisonKey` already is that seam (the other two now mirror it).

Now each identifier has one obvious place where the hashed value is decided — a uniform, one-line insertion point for the `'V2'` tag.

- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.emitOwnerCreatedAudit`** — split the structured `OwnerCreatedEvent` construction out into a private `ownerCreatedEvent(owner, ownerDto)` builder (matching the file's existing single-accessor style, e.g. `primaryIdentifier`). The audit-schema-v2 additions (`schemaVersion`, a recomputed owner segment sourced from the injected `ownerMapper`) now have a focused home instead of piling into the emit method — which also removes the need for a duplicated segment method in the controller.

## What I deliberately left alone

The `OwnerMapper::apiVersion` / `OwnerMapper::identity` hotspots and the audit's `schemaVersion` are inherently **schema-coupled** (the generated `OwnerDto` and `OwnerCreatedEvent` don't have those fields yet). Adding them now would add fields to the response/event and thus change behavior, so they belong to the change itself, not to this preparation.

## Verification

The created-owner response is **byte-identical** to the pre-refactor baseline across every derived field (`memberId NSW2716E6609E1`, `householdId 11b2b2a3a9a7`, `identityKey df28…`, `locality NSW`, `fiscalYear FY27`, `ownerSegment STANDARD_METRO`, `timezone Australia/Sydney`). Everything compiles, and `AcceptanceTest` still fails on exactly the same `$.apiVersion` assertion — no regression, behavior preserved.
